notes: PC-first spSkin runtime and spSkinSerializer read/write cycle; PS2 deliberately deferred because PC evidence was sufficient.

classes.summary: PC identity, full observed member extent, ownership/copy, renderer palette submission and the matching serializer contract are reconstructed; constructor defaults, exact matrix convention, full portable stream mutation and PS2 remain open.

evidence.observation: The PC object has weightCount at +0x60, boneCount at +0x64, spNode pointer array at +0x68 and parallel 64-byte matrix array at +0x6C; destructor frees both arrays and copy remaps relationships.
The render body combines bone transforms with inverse-bind matrices, publishes the palette count to the renderer, submits the inherited base mesh and clears temporary palette state.
Pinned-executable body hashes, vtables, offsets, target ID, serializer entry points and source path pass 21 independent regression checks.
Portable ownership, clone/copy and palette invariants compile and pass the project CTest suite; analytical API names are kept distinct from unknown originals.

classes.summary: PC identity, source path, storage-free layout, target class, index/write/read bodies and null-bone error branch are reconstructed; full portable stream/fixup/rollback execution and PS2 remain open.

evidence.observation: spSkinSerializer directly derives from spModelSerializer, adds no observed storage beyond 0x14, targets spSkin and preserves the exact original translation-unit path.
Index traverses all bones; writer and reader agree on two UInt32 values followed by one spNode relationship and one 64-byte inverse-bind matrix per slot, and reader rejects null bones.
The portable serializer exposes only the confirmed field and payload plan while leaving object-directory mutation to the still-incomplete common serializer protocol.
